correction01.p1BoundaryContract: CONFIRMED AND CORRECTED. The retained-tail counterexample reproduces (inferred boundary 3 vs authoritative 5), and the display-only divergence reproduces (Phase A passed 3 vs persisted 2). The production Phase-A boundary now uses countCanonicalSourceMessages(context.messages), which is the SAME filter createSessionCompactionState() applies, so the persisted section and the persisted boundary agree by construction. The inference's unsupported 'exact for every real production shape' claim is WITHDRAWN and replaced with the honest, CONSERVATIVE contract: the inference can UNDER-estimate the boundary, so the section can only be a subset of the boundary's outcomes.
correction01.p2BudgetRationale: CONFIRMED AND CORRECTED. The 'boundary-scoped ledger is a subset of the whole-history ledger, so the request can only shrink' argument was MATHEMATICALLY FALSE: the ledger retains the most RECENT 12 outcomes, so a boundary-scoped ledger can retain older and, when they render longer, LARGER entries. Measured: 632 bytes (whole) vs 656 bytes (scoped). The argument is WITHDRAWN and replaced with the actual authority - the FINAL budget guard at the provider-dispatch seam (agent-runtime.ts, assertProviderRequestWithinBudget()), which measures the provider-visible projection of the FINAL messages after every beforeModel mutation and FAILS CLOSED with TaskContractBudgetError before any provider dispatch. The repair does not change that guard.
correction01.p2FinalArtifactIdentity: CORRECTED. The head identities are now explicit: subjectHead (the implementation commit), artifactHead (the commit that produced the original artifact package) and finalHead (the ACT's terminal commit).
correction01.productionBehaviourChanged: Only the Phase-A boundary value, and only when a display-only message is present in the canonical history. The retained-tail shape never reached the production path: all three production call sites pass an explicit boundary, so the inference is a fallback for direct helper calls only.

correction02.p0CanonicalCountOnUnfilteredArray: CONFIRMED, REPRODUCED and FIXED. The boundary ledger was extracted with `canonicalMessages.slice(0, boundaryCount)` over the RAW list, while `boundaryCount` is a CANONICAL count. Each display-only message preceding the boundary consumed one slice slot, so the prefix ended early and dropped a verified outcome that was genuinely INSIDE the boundary. Measured: carriedOutcomeCount 0, EVIDENCE LOST, in BOTH Phase A and Phase B. The dropped outcome is before the canonical tail, so nothing else restored it — a correctness failure, not a compactness one. FIXED: `canonicalSourceMessages()` is exported and applied BEFORE the slice, so the count and the slice operate over the identical ordered collection.
correction02.p1FallbackNeverCorrectnessClaim: CONFIRMED and WITHDRAWN. Measured: an under-estimated boundary can OMIT a boundary outcome (the section carried zero outcomes). The contract is narrowed: the inference is safe for FABRICATION but NOT for OMISSION, so it is an APPROXIMATION that is not authoritative for evidence conservation. The production path is unaffected — all three call sites pass an explicit boundary.
correction02.p1BudgetGuardOrderingClaim: CONFIRMED wrong and CORRECTED. The compaction path calls `saveState` INTERNALLY (compaction.ts:1618 for Phase A, :1715 for re-compaction) and only then returns to the dispatch path. PERSISTENCE safety (the compaction-side budget projection, before the sidecar is written) is now stated separately from DISPATCH safety (the final provider-request guard in agent-runtime.ts, which fails closed before any provider request leaves the process). Both fail closed; neither is changed.
correction02.p2Rolling12SubsetTerminology: CORRECTED. Every surviving use of 'subset' refers to the BOUNDARY's own outcomes, never to the whole-history ledger, whose rolling-12 window invalidates that relation.
correction02.productionBehaviourChanged: Only the boundary ledger's SOURCE COLLECTION: it is now the canonical collection instead of the raw list. In a history WITHOUT a display-only message the two collections are identical, so the behaviour is unchanged.
